You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:

CREATE TABLE course (
    Course_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Staring_Date TEXT,
    Course TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Course_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE teacher (
    Teacher_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Age TEXT,
    Hometown TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Teacher_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE course_arrange (
    Course_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Teacher_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Grade INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    PRIMARY KEY (Course_ID, Teacher_ID, Grade),
    UNIQUE (Course_ID, Teacher_ID, Grade),
    FOREIGN KEY (Teacher_ID) REFERENCES teacher(Teacher_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Course_ID) REFERENCES course(Course_ID)
);

When you have a final SQL query to present, always wrap it in a sql markdown code fence like this:

```sql
SELECT ...
```

This makes it easy to identify your answer. Only use one ```sql fence for your final query.

Do you mean a combined datasheet listing courses, start dates, assigned teachers and grades? If so, use this query — it returns each course with its start date, grade, and teacher details. Tell me if you want different columns, filters (by grade, teacher, or date), or CSV output.

```sql
SELECT
  c.Course_ID,
  c.Course,
  c.Staring_Date,
  ca.Grade,
  t.Teacher_ID,
  t.Name    AS Teacher_Name,
  t.Age     AS Teacher_Age,
  t.Hometown AS Teacher_Hometown
FROM course_arrange ca
JOIN course c ON ca.Course_ID = c.Course_ID
JOIN teacher t ON ca.Teacher_ID = t.Teacher_ID
ORDER BY c.Staring_Date, c.Course, ca.Grade;
```
make sure the list shows which courses each teacher is in charge of

```sql
SELECT
  t.Teacher_ID,
  t.Name           AS Teacher_Name,
  t.Age            AS Teacher_Age,
  t.Hometown       AS Teacher_Hometown,
  COUNT(c.Course_ID) AS Course_Count,
  GROUP_CONCAT(
    DISTINCT c.Course || ' (Course_ID=' || c.Course_ID || ', Grade=' || IFNULL(ca.Grade, 'N/A') || ', Start=' || IFNULL(c.Staring_Date, 'N/A') || ')'
    , '; '
  ) AS Courses_In_Charge
FROM teacher t
LEFT JOIN course_arrange ca ON t.Teacher_ID = ca.Teacher_ID
LEFT JOIN course c         ON ca.Course_ID = c.Course_ID
GROUP BY t.Teacher_ID, t.Name, t.Age, t.Hometown
ORDER BY t.Name;
```
make it so only teacher names and their courses are shown.

```sql
SELECT
  t.Name AS Teacher_Name,
  COALESCE(GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT c.Course, ', '), 'None') AS Courses
FROM teacher t
LEFT JOIN course_arrange ca ON t.Teacher_ID = ca.Teacher_ID
LEFT JOIN course c ON ca.Course_ID = c.Course_ID
GROUP BY t.Teacher_ID, t.Name
ORDER BY t.Name;
```
make sure the list is sorted by teacher names alphabetically

```sql
SELECT
  t.Name AS Teacher_Name,
  COALESCE(GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT c.Course, ', '), 'None') AS Courses
FROM teacher t
LEFT JOIN course_arrange ca ON t.Teacher_ID = ca.Teacher_ID
LEFT JOIN course c ON ca.Course_ID = c.Course_ID
GROUP BY t.Teacher_ID, t.Name
ORDER BY t.Name COLLATE NOCASE ASC;
```
